title: [precompile] Add DynamoTracer and serve its captures through capture()
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #198217
* #198227
* __->__ #198138
* #198216
* #198137
* #198215
* #198136
* #198214
* #198243
* #198135
* #198213
* #197993
* #198284
* #198283
* #198223
* #198211

**Problem.** `torch.compiler.precompile.capture()` only took a `MakeFxTracer`: one positional call, one ATen trace, no graph breaks, no recompiled variants, no keyword arguments. The `PrecompileSession` of the previous commits can record all of those, but nothing in the public module reached it.

**Fix.** Add `DynamoTracer`, the multi-graph front-end passed as `tracer=`, and `_DynamoCapture`, the `Capture` that drives a `PrecompileSession` across as many calls as the block makes and writes the standalone artifact on a clean exit, so `load()` serves it in a fresh process.

**Summary.** `capture()` accepted a `MakeFxTracer` and nothing else, so a function with a graph break, a shape-dependent branch or a keyword argument could not be precompiled through `torch.compiler.precompile` even though `PrecompileSession` and `snapshot_artifact` could already record and render such captures. This commit adds `DynamoTracer(guard_filter_fn, recompile_limit, dynamic, require_complete, require_no_risky_drops, require_no_dropped_guards)` beside `MakeFxTracer`, and `_DynamoCapture`, which enters the session under a fresh `CacheArtifactManager` cache so the inductor bundle in the cache half holds only this capture's compiles (the swap spans the whole block, which the `capture()` docstring now states), counts attempted calls so a block whose calls all raised gets the `require_complete` report rather than "nothing was captured", refuses a recursive re-entry, and on a clean exit renders the pair behind the three `require_*` gates and writes it, while a block that raised writes nothing and a gate refusal is raised after teardown with nothing written. The artifact is standalone, so `fn` must be a module-level function of an importable module, an artifact whose capture graph-broke cannot load beside the live compile that captured it (the continuation names collide, and `load` says so), and it is locked to the producing Python version and torch build. A Dynamo capture runs every call in the caller's grad mode and lowers a backward whenever grad is enabled, so a training step that calls `.backward()` captures its compiled backward and the served artifact accumulates `.grad` like eager, which a fresh-process test checks on both backends. `MakeFxTracer` stays the default for two more commits, package and recompile errors surface as `PrecompileError`, and mid-block `save()` checkpoints and `summary()` are the next commit's, so `save()` on this tracer raises a `PrecompileError` saying its artifact is written when the block exits.

## Where this fits

The stack replaces the callable `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` (trace once on inputs passed up front, pair returned in memory) with a caller-driven context manager: `capture(fn, artifact_path=, cache_path=)` is entered with a `with` block, the caller calls it on as many example inputs as they like (each graph break and recompiled variant is folded in), the `(python_code, cache)` pair is written to the two files on exit, and `load(artifact_path, cache_path)` serves it in a fresh process. The end-to-end example and the PR-by-PR map live in #197993's "The new API, end to end" section. This PR is where `capture()` becomes multi-call: `DynamoTracer` takes as many calls as the caller makes and folds every graph break and recompile they exercise into one artifact. It becomes the default tracer in #198217.

## The golden path

The new tests write a module with a graph-breaking step, capture it over two shapes and a keyword default, and serve it in a fresh process:

```python
# precompile_golden_<uuid>.py, importable from sys.path
def step(model, x, *, scale=1.0):
    y = model(x) * scale * SCALE
    torch._dynamo.graph_break()
    if y.shape[0] > 2:
        y = y + 1
    return y.sum(dim=0)
```

```python
from torch.compiler.precompile import capture, DynamoTracer, load

with capture(step, artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache", tracer=DynamoTracer(), backend="inductor") as cap:
    y2 = cap(model, x2)               # step and its graph-break continuation
    y3 = cap(model, x3, scale=0.5)    # the branch recompiles the continuation; the keyword is a second entry variant
# exit: TRACER = "dynamo", SERVING_MODE = "standalone", FN_NAME = 'step' in m.py

load("m.py", "m.cache")               # in this process: PrecompileError, the message says to use a fresh process
```

```python
# a fresh process
f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache")
f(model, x2)                          # == y2
f(model, x3, scale=0.5)               # == y3
f(model, x2.double())                 # PrecompileError: no captured variant
```

The last line is the standalone contract: there is no compiler behind a source artifact, so a call no variant covers raises rather than silently serving. `test_graph_breaks_and_recompiles_round_trip_in_a_fresh_process` pins this on both backends, including the in-process collision refusal; `test_a_single_graph_serves_in_process` pins the no-graph-break case, where `load` works in the capturing process, `f.installed` is false, `with f:` and `f.unload()` are no-ops, a second `Model()` swaps weights in, and `f(model, x3)` after a shape-2 capture raises `no captured variant`.

## `DynamoTracer` carries the multi-graph knobs

```python
@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class DynamoTracer:
    guard_filter_fn: Callable[[Sequence[Any]], Sequence[bool]] | None = None
    recompile_limit: int = 256
    dynamic: bool | None = None
    require_complete: bool = True
    require_no_risky_drops: bool = True
    require_no_dropped_guards: bool = False
```

`guard_filter_fn` filters the guards kept in the serialized artifact (runtime capture guards are always retained; the default drops only what cannot be serialized), `recompile_limit` caps recompilations per frame, and `dynamic` forces dynamic shapes as `torch.compile(dynamic=)` does. The `require_*` gates refuse, at write time, an artifact with a coverage gap (`require_complete`: a bypassed or uncovered frame, a call that raised), one whose dropped guards told captured variants apart or hang off a configuration-chosen slot (`require_no_risky_drops`), or one that dropped any guard at all (`require_no_dropped_guards`, off by default since every model drops identity guards that cannot be serialized). The docstring names what `guard_filter_fn` receives: the `GuardFilterEntry` records (`guard_type`, `name`, ...), returning one keep flag per entry. The annotation stays `Sequence[Any]` rather than naming `GuardFilterEntry`, because torch/compiler/precompile.py resolves the re-homed classes' annotations with `typing.get_type_hints` at import.

`test_the_tracer_knobs_reach_the_session` pins that the knobs get through to the session: a `DynamoTracer(dynamic=True)` capture of `single` on `x2` serves `x3` too, and a `guard_filter_fn` that drops the guard on `x` on top of `default_guard_filter_fn` (dropping what tells the shapes apart) is refused by `require_no_risky_drops` (`can affect dispatch`), while the same filter with `require_no_risky_drops=False` writes an artifact that loads. `DynamoTracer(dynamic=False, recompile_limit=1)` called on `x2` then `x3` keeps only the first shape's variant, so the served artifact refuses `x3` with `no captured variant`. `test_the_strict_gate_refuses_dropped_guards` shows the default capture of `single` listing `['MODULE_MATCH', ...` in the artifact's dropped guards, and `DynamoTracer(require_no_dropped_guards=True)` refusing the same capture with a `dropped ... guard` error.

## `capture()` dispatches on the tracer

```python
tracer: MakeFxTracer | DynamoTracer = MakeFxTracer()
...
if isinstance(tracer, MakeFxTracer):
    return _MakeFxCapture(fn, artifact_path, cache_path, backend=backend, decompositions=tracer.decompositions)
if not isinstance(tracer, DynamoTracer):
    raise TypeError("precompile.capture tracer must be a MakeFxTracer or DynamoTracer, got ...")
if backend not in ("inductor", "eager"):
    raise ValueError(f"precompile backend must be 'inductor' or 'eager', got {backend!r}.")
try:
    session = precompile_capture(fn, backend=backend, guard_filter_fn=tracer.guard_filter_fn, recompile_limit=tracer.recompile_limit, dynamic=tracer.dynamic)
except PackageError as e:
    raise PrecompileError(str(e)) from e
return _DynamoCapture(session, artifact_path, cache_path, require_complete=..., require_no_risky_drops=..., require_no_dropped_guards=...)
```

The make_fx front-end validates `backend` when it builds its `PrecompiledModule`; the Dynamo front-end builds none, so `capture()` checks it before creating the session. `precompile_capture`'s up-front refusals now surface as `PrecompileError`, which `test_entries_a_standalone_artifact_cannot_rebuild_are_refused` pins: a bare `nn.Module` (`CALLS the model`: Dynamo compiles its wrapper frame, whose graphs close over the module) and a closure entry (`closes over`), since a code object cannot rebuild what the closure captured. A `functools.partial` never reaches the tracer: `capture()` itself refuses it with a `TypeError` (`takes the function itself, not a functools.partial`) before dispatching, and the same test asserts that `TypeError`. `_MakeFxCapture`'s two refusals (a keyword argument, a second call) now point at `tracer=DynamoTracer()` instead of just explaining themselves.

## `_DynamoCapture` drives the session

Entering the block opens a fresh cache before the session, and undoes it if the session refuses to enter:

```python
def __enter__(self):
    with self._lock:
        if self._call is not None or self._exited:
            raise PrecompileError("this capture has already been entered; capture() returns a fresh capture per call.")
        self._fresh_cache = CacheArtifactManager.with_fresh_cache()
        self._fresh_cache.__enter__()
        try:
            self._call = self._map(self._session.__enter__)
        except BaseException:
            self._fresh_cache.__exit__(None, None, None)
            self._fresh_cache = None
            raise
    return self
```

The capture's compiles record into the process-global cache-artifact list, which the cache half of the artifact bundles to prime the kernel caches on load; a fresh one means the bundle holds only this capture's compiles. The swap spans the whole `with` block, not just the calls, so anything else compiled inside the block records into the same list; the `capture()` docstring now says a `DynamoTracer` capture records the kernel-cache artifacts of everything compiled inside the block, so compile nothing else there and do not overlap two such captures. `_map` is the one place `PackageError` and `RecompileError` become `PrecompileError`. Each call is serialized under an `RLock`, refuses a call before `__enter__` or after `__exit__` (`capture is not active`), refuses `fn` calling the capture it is being captured through (`re-entered recursively`), and counts the call before it runs:

```python
def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
    with self._lock:
        ...
        self._in_call = True
        # Counted before the call: a call that raised is for the session's
        # require_complete gate to report, not "nothing was captured".
        self._calls += 1
        try:
            return self._map(self._call, *args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            self._in_call = False
```

Counting attempts rather than successes matters for a block whose only calls raised: it made calls, so exit goes on to `snapshot_artifact`, and the session's `require_complete` report lists the capture errors instead of the misleading `nothing was captured`.

Exit writes on a clean block only, and holds a gate refusal until the session and cache are torn down:

```python
def __exit__(self, *exc):
    with self._lock:
        error = None
        try:
            if exc[0] is None:
                try:
                    if self._calls == 0:
                        raise PrecompileError("nothing was captured: call the capture with your example arguments inside the `with` block.")
                    self._write()        # snapshot_artifact(**gates) then _write_artifact(...)
                except BaseException as e:
                    error = e
            self._exited = True
            try:
                self._map(self._session.__exit__, *exc)
            except BaseException as e:
                if error is None:
                    raise
                raise e from error
        finally:
            if self._fresh_cache is not None:
                self._fresh_cache.__exit__(None, None, None)
                self._fresh_cache = None
    if exc[0] is None and error is not None:
        raise error
```

A teardown error that follows a gate refusal is raised `from` the refusal, so the refusal is not lost, and the fresh cache is always exited with `(None, None, None)` rather than with the in-flight exception. `_write` renders through `self._session.snapshot_artifact(**self._gates)` and hands the pair to `_write_artifact`; an `OSError` there becomes a `PrecompileError` (`precompile could not write the artifact`), and since `_write_artifact` leaves the previous pair in place the last good pair is still loadable. `test_a_raised_call_is_refused_at_exit_and_writes_nothing` pins the gate: a second call with `torch.randn(2, 5)` into a `Linear(4, 4)` raises `RuntimeError` inside the block, the block itself runs to completion, exit raises `PrecompileError` (`captured call raised`) through `require_complete`, and neither `m.py` nor `m.cache` exists afterwards. The same test covers a block whose only call raised, which reaches the same `captured call raised` gate rather than `nothing was captured`, and `DynamoTracer(require_complete=False)`, which writes the partial artifact instead.

`test_misuse_is_refused` pins the rest of the lifecycle: a bad backend (`backend="aot_eager"`) raises `ValueError`, an unknown tracer (`tracer=object()`) raises `TypeError` (`tracer must be`), a call before the block raises `not active`, an empty block raises `nothing was captured`, a second `with` on the same capture raises `already been entered`, a call after it raises `not active` again, a `Reentrant` module whose `forward` calls the capture raises `re-entered recursively`, a block raising its own `KeyError` propagates it unchanged and writes nothing, and a mocked `_write_artifact` raising `OSError` surfaces as `PrecompileError` (`could not write`).

## Grad mode and the training step

`capture()` has no grad-mode flag. A Dynamo capture runs every call in the caller's own grad mode and lowers a backward whenever grad is enabled: a `.backward()` in `fn` graph-breaks and re-runs at serve time through the live autograd engine, accumulating `.grad` like eager, so a training step is captured like any other call, and the artifact should be served under the grad mode it was captured in.

```python
def train_step(model, x):
    model(x).sum().backward()

with capture(train_step, ..., tracer=DynamoTracer(), backend=backend) as cap:   # backend: "inductor" or "eager"
    cap(model, x2)                    # returns None; model.lin.weight.grad matches an eager step

# a fresh process, model reloaded from the pre-step state dict
f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache")
f(model, x2)                          # returns None; every parameter's .grad matches the eager step
```

`test_training_step_grads_match_eager_in_a_fresh_process`, parametrized over `inductor` and `eager`, is what pins the claim that the served artifact accumulates `.grad` like eager: it runs an eager step on a `Model` loaded from the same state dict, checks the capture's `lin.weight` grad against it, restores the pre-step weights, and serves the artifact in a fresh process, asserting each parameter's `.grad` against the eager one.

## The artifact does not mix with a make_fx pair

`test_a_dynamo_pair_does_not_mix_with_a_make_fx_pair` captures `single` once with `DynamoTracer()` and once with `MakeFxTracer()` into two pairs; `load` of the Dynamo artifact with the make_fx cache raises `PrecompileError` mentioning `tracer`, and the reverse raises `tracer` or `does not match`. `load`'s docstring now says a Dynamo artifact takes keyword arguments, that entering and unloading it are no-ops, that it re-seeds the names Dynamo minted into the captured module, and that an artifact whose capture graph-broke must be loaded in a fresh process.

## Exports, docs and scope

`DynamoTracer` joins `torch.compiler.precompile.__all__`, the `__module__` re-homing loop, the public-members test, and the API reference (`.. autoclass:: torch.compiler.precompile.DynamoTracer` in docs/source/torch.compiler_api.md). `MakeFxTracer` stays the default for two more commits; the tests pass `tracer=DynamoTracer()` explicitly through `_capture`. Mid-block `save()` checkpoints and the `summary()` report are the next commit's (#198227), so `_DynamoCapture.save()` raises `PrecompileError` (`save() is not supported on a DynamoTracer capture yet: its artifact is written when the block exits.`) rather than the base class's bare `NotImplementedError`. The module Note's `tracer:` paragraph now describes both tracers (`MakeFxTracer` the default, `DynamoTracer` standalone and version-locked, refusing uncovered calls through its guards and listing the guards it could not serialize as `DROPPED_GUARDS`) instead of saying `dynamo` raises `NotImplementedError`. Deliberately absent, as follow-ups: the installed serving mode (`load(fn=)`), the rendered-as-source subgraphs, the invariants report and the per-frame drift probe. The fresh-process tests are skipped under the crossref harness, whose active dispatch mode Dynamo guards on and a fresh process lacks.

Test Plan:

`TestPrecompileDynamoCapture` in test/test_precompile.py, passing `tracer=DynamoTracer()` explicitly: the graph-break/recompile round trip through a fresh process on both backends (with the in-process collision refusal), a single-graph capture served in process (weight swap, no-op enter/unload, uncovered call), a training step on both backends served in a fresh process whose `.grad` matches eager, the raised-call gate at exit (including a block whose only call raised, and `require_complete=False` writing the partial artifact), the misuse refusals (bad backend or tracer, a call outside the block, a re-entered or recursive capture, an empty block, a block raising its own exception, a write failure), the `dynamic`, `guard_filter_fn`, `require_no_risky_drops` and `recompile_limit` knobs, the strict dropped-guard gate, the module/closure/partial refusals, and the make_fx/dynamo pair mismatch. The fresh-process tests are skipped under the crossref harness, whose active dispatch mode Dynamo guards on and a fresh process lacks.

```

PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_CROSSREF=1 python test/test_precompile.py -k TestPrecompileDynamoCapture
lintrunner -a torch/_precompile.py torch/compiler/precompile.py test/test_precompile.py docs/source/torch.compiler_api.md
```

title: [dynamo] Validate getattr arguments before dispatch
body:
## Summary

Part of #195901.

`GetAttrBuiltinVariable` accessed positional arguments before validating `getattr()` calls. Too few arguments could raise an internal `IndexError`, excess arguments could be silently ignored, and keyword arguments were not rejected before dispatch. Non-string attribute names could also surface as internal Dynamo errors.

This change uses `no_keywords` and `check_positional` to match CPython’s argument validation, validates attribute names before generic lookup, adds focused regression coverage for invalid calls, and removes the CPython 3.13 expected-failure marker for `BuiltinTest.test_getattr`.

title: [dynamo] Fix random.shuffle/random.sample freezing across repeated compiled calls
body:
Fixes #197085

## Summary

Inside a `torch.compile`d function, module-level `random.shuffle`/`random.sample` returned the same result on every call after the first, instead of drawing fresh each call like eager and like the other supported `random.*` functions (`random()`, `randint()`, `randrange()`, `uniform()`) already do.

**Root cause:** `RandomVariable.shuffle`/`sample` computed the permutation against a trace-time-only `random.Random` snapshot and baked the result into the graph as a constant. The scalar random functions instead route through Dynamo's existing "recorded call, re-executed on every real invocation" mechanism (`tx.output.random_calls`, replayed via `_get_gen_rand_values_fn`), which `shuffle`/`sample` never used.

**Fix:** add a `GlobalRandomVariable(RandomVariable)` subclass, selected at construction time when the wrapped `random.Random` is the actual process-global instance (`random._inst`). It overrides `shuffle`, `sample`, `seed`, `setstate` and `_call_random` to route through the same `random_calls` replay mechanism, so real values are drawn fresh on every invocation instead of being frozen at trace time. Explicit `random.Random()` instances keep the prior trace-time-only behavior unchanged.

The runtime-replay path is restricted to populations that are fully constant-foldable and homogeneous in a runtime-primitive type (`bool`/`int`/`float`); anything else (tensors, strings, mixed non-numeric types) falls back to the original trace-time-only behavior. This avoids two failure modes found during review:

- A population with heterogeneous element types could have its trace-time-chosen and real-runtime-chosen types diverge at a given list position, and Dynamo skips the `TYPE_MATCH` guard for these sources, so a mismatch was reaching `torch.tensor()` uncaught (`TypeError: new(): invalid data type 'str'`).
- Treating a non-numeric runtime-replayed value as a plain `ConstantVariable` risks Dynamo elsewhere treating it as a genuine compile-time constant (e.g. for branching), when its real value can differ on every call.

The fallback path also records its own state-advancing closure into `random_calls` (rather than relying solely on the end-of-function side-effect mutation replay), since that mutation replay runs after `random_calls` is already replayed each invocation -- without this, a fallback shuffle/sample sharing a compiled function with any other `random_calls`-routed call (a plain `random()`, another `seed()`, etc.) would leave that other call frozen too.

## Test Plan

  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_object_shuffle \

  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_module_shuffle_sample \
  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_module_shuffle_sample_tensor_list \
  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_module_shuffle_heterogeneous_list \
  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_module_shuffle_sample_nonnumeric_fallback \
  test.dynamo.test_unspec.UnspecTests.test_random_module_shuffle_sample_mixed_numeric_types_fallback \

title: [dynamo] Graph break on shape-changing differentiable Tensor.data assignment
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #186512

DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 style forward hooks gather partitioned parameters by
assigning a full-sized tensor to Parameter.data before a submodule runs,
then repartition the same parameter back to an empty tensor in a forward
hook. Dynamo traced those hook-side mutations into the same graph as the
module compute.

AOTAutograd builds backward graphs from the original metadata of differentiable
graph inputs. If a traced .data assignment changes an input's shape, later
forward operations can produce gradients with the replacement shape for an
input whose original shape is different, causing an invalid-gradient failure.
This invariant applies to ordinary differentiable tensors as well as Parameters.

Fix this by graph breaking before shape-changing .data mutations on
differentiable tensors. Fake shapes are compared with sym_eq and
statically_known_true, so symbolic equality is not guarded and unbacked SymInts
are not evaluated. If equality cannot be proven, Dynamo conservatively breaks;
provably same symbolic shapes and non-differentiable assignments remain
traceable. The check does not depend on ambient grad mode because a mutation
inside a local no_grad block can be followed by differentiable use.

A fully traced alternative would require AOTAutograd-safe semantics for changing
differentiable input metadata. This patch uses the narrower correctness
boundary and lets Dynamo resume on the tensor compute after the mutation.

Fixes #115484

title: [Dynamo] Detect tensor mutations when reconstructing generators
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #185920

Dynamo reconstructs returned local generators by exhausting the remaining generator body during bytecode generation. Existing generator reconstruction side-effect checks rejected Python object mutations, but two paths still missed tensor data mutation: direct generator returns exhausted the generator without entering the reconstruction guard, and tensor writes were represented as FX tensor operations rather than normal SideEffects mutations.

This wraps direct returned-generator exhaustion in the generator reconstruction guard and teaches tensor operation paths to reject tensor writes while that guard is active. The detection covers mutating tensor methods, torch function schemas that write the first tensor argument, out= tensors, in-place builtin operators such as +=, and version-change based in-place mutations.

I considered relying only on fake tensor version changes after tracing, but some paths need to stop before graph insertion or before fake propagation mutates out= metadata. The schema checks keep the rejection close to each mutating entry point while still using the existing SideEffects error path.

Fixes #146628

title: Anchor a property descriptor's guard source at the type
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #196154
* #196153
* #196152
* #196940
* #196939
* #196938
* #196150
* #196151
* __->__ #197585

`object_generic_getattr` computes one instance-anchored source and hands it to
`_resolve_descriptor_get` for every kind of descriptor. That anchor is wrong
for a `property`: the descriptor lives on the type, and `PropertyVariable`
derives its `fget` source from it, so the guard reads `L['obj'].attr.fget` --
which evaluates the getter and then asks the resulting value for `.fget`:

    AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fget'

Reaching it takes a `property` on an object Dynamo wraps as a
`ConstantVariable`, which in practice means `torch.cuda._CudaDeviceProperties`:

```python
props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
torch.compile(lambda x: x + props.multi_processor_count)(torch.randn(2, device="cuda"))
```

Point the source at the descriptor `mro_lookup` actually returned. Naming it
`type(obj).attr` is not enough: that reads back through `type.__getattribute__`,
where a data descriptor on the metaclass beats the class chain, so a metaclass
`property` of the same name reproduces the very same `.fget` error one level up.
Index the owning class's `__dict__` instead, walking the MRO to find it and
guarding that the classes ahead of it still do not define the name.

Only the `property` branch moves: `staticmethod` and `classmethod` keep the
instance anchor, since reading those through the type unwraps them. A
pure-Python property resolves through `UserDefinedObjectVariable` and never gets
here, and `torch.finfo` / `torch.iinfo` expose getset descriptors rather than
properties.

That MRO walk already existed three times over -- in
`AutogradFunctionVariable._get_raw_attribute_source` and in both
`get_source_by_walking_mro` methods -- so it becomes one `mro_attr_source` next
to `mro_lookup`, and the callers keep only what differs: their extra guard and
what a miss means. Three discrepancies had to be settled to share it. The
absent-guard loop runs `range(idx)` everywhere now, so the `user_defined`
callers guard MRO index 0 the way `misc` already did -- otherwise setting the
attribute on `type(obj)` later moves the owner while the guard still reads
`__mro__[idx]`. `mro_source_cache` is keyed on the owning class rather than the
descriptor: one descriptor object can sit in several unrelated classes, and a
source through one of them does not notice the attribute being reassigned on
another. Keying on the owner still lets instances and subclasses that reach the
same owner share one source, so they do not pick up an OBJECT_ALIASING guard.
And entry 0 is spelled as the class itself only after checking that it is the
class -- every MRO CPython computes puts it there, but a metaclass overriding
`mro()` can not, and now that index 0 is guarded the mismatch would fail a guard
on the frame that created it.

`TestConstantTypeProperty` covers the `common_constant_types` path: a plain
property, one shadowed by a metaclass descriptor, one inherited from a base,
one shadowed on the subclass after the first compile (which has to recompile),
and one on a class whose metaclass reorders `__mro__`. The
`_CudaDeviceProperties` case moves to `TestConstantTypePropertyAccelerator`, so
both classes carry a `hw_classification` and survive `--hw-classification`.
Two tests in `test_repros.py` pin the cache key from both sides: a descriptor
shared by unrelated classes recompiles when one of them reassigns it, and two
instances reaching the same class attribute get no OBJECT_ALIASING guard.

Test Plan:

```shell
python -m pytest test/dynamo/test_user_defined_object.py
python -m pytest test/dynamo/test_misc.py test/dynamo/test_repros.py \

title: Preserve input aliases for multi-output view returns
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #186503

AOTAutograd classified differentiable multi-output views of graph inputs as
non-alias outputs. All siblings then shared one `CompiledFunctionBackward`, so
backward on the first output freed saved state required by later outputs.

This change keeps those results as input aliases and reconstructs their eager
view graph outside the compiled autograd function. To avoid quadratic replay, it
groups outputs by the exact shared autograd view node, finds the last
multi-output operation in each chain, replays that operation once, and applies
each sibling's own suffix views. The implementation supports both saved
functionalization `ViewMeta` recipes and autograd `ViewFunc` chains, including
prefixes, heterogeneous multi-operation suffixes, reordered/subset results, and
independent identical calls.

Symbolic view recipes may be removed before cache serialization, so trace-time
lazy conjugate/negative metadata is retained and restored with differentiable
view operations during fallback. When synthetic bases replace input views, stale
recipes relative to the pre-merge input are discarded. Metadata mutations retain
their logical version ordering so regenerated views remain valid, while inference
tensors and failed compiled calls preserve their expected version behavior.

The existing optimization for views of computed intermediates remains intact.
Nested multi-output chains batch their last shared operation; fully memoizing
earlier multi-output prefixes across independent inner groups is intentionally
left as a broader optimization.

Fixes #118739

title: Prevent saving mutated grad inputs in AOT min-cut
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #185876

AOTAutograd clones data-mutated grad inputs in the joint trace so the
backward graph can read their pre-mutation values. For mutations replayed by
the runtime epilogue, the original primal placeholder is not a valid saved
activation: it aliases the user's input and is mutated after the AOT forward
returns, so backward can observe a bumped version counter.

Mark only grad-requiring primal inputs whose data mutation is
`MUTATED_OUT_GRAPH`, and make min-cut treat those placeholders as unsaveable.
Mutations kept inside the graph, including conservative hidden mutations from
custom Triton kernels, remain valid saved inputs. This distinction fixes the
original failure without making such graphs produce an infeasible min-cut.
The zero-budget input-only fast path remains in place unless an out-of-graph
mutation needs a safe cut.

Catching the resulting `NetworkXUnbounded` or suppressing its visualization
would only mask the incorrect constraint, so the fix narrows the mutation
classification at its source.

Fixes #185497

title: [Feature Refactoring][dynamo] Device-agnostic repro generation in after_aot for out-of-tree backends
body:
## Summary

`torch/_dynamo/repro/after_aot.py` hardcodes CUDA in four places, which blocks out-of-tree accelerator backends from using the repro tooling: generated repro scripts only do `import torch` (so a PrivateUse1 backend fails when the script recreates tensors on that device), the repro header calls `_cuda_system_info_comment()` (CUDA toolchain info only), `repro_minify` pins subprocesses with `torch.cuda.device_count()` + `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and a helper infers the carrier device with `tensor.is_cuda`. This PR makes all four device-agnostic with zero new public API, reusing the `arg.device.type != "cpu"` inverse check already used elsewhere in this file. All probing happens at call time — no import-time side effects (this module sits on the torch_npu import chain via `torch/_inductor/debug.py`, so import-time purity is mandatory).

## Changes

- Added a module-private helper `_infer_repro_device_type(args)` that returns the device type of the first non-cpu tensor argument (or "cpu").
- The repro header system info keeps `_cuda_system_info_comment()` verbatim for cpu/cuda and falls back to generic `getattr`-based collection for other accelerators (`torch.version.<dt>`, `is_available`, `device_count`, `get_device_name`). Every failure degrades to comment text — debug tooling must never break repro generation.
- Added `_oot_backend_imports(device_type)`: injects `try: import torch_<backend>` into the generated script only when the device type equals the registered PrivateUse1 backend name (`torch._C._get_privateuse1_backend_name()`); built-in devices inject nothing.
- Added `_minifier_env_variables(args)`: resolves the visibility env var through a small device-type mapping (currently `{"npu": "ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES"}`; `TODO(#189137)` — switch to the future DeviceInterface API when it lands). CPU, cuda and any unmapped device type keep the historical `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` lines verbatim; `repro_minify` now calls it.
- Extended `test/dynamo/test_after_aot.py` with a new `TestAfterAotDeviceDecoupling` class (`@instantiate_parametrized_tests`, `hw_classification = HardwareClassification.GENERIC`, 13 tests including a `@parametrize`-driven mapping test and an `hpu` unmapped-type fallback case). Tests call the production symbols directly; mocks are used only for determinism (patching `torch.npu`, `torch._C._get_privateuse1_backend_name`, `torch.cuda.device_count`).

| device | repro header info | generated script | minifier env |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cuda | `_cuda_system_info_comment()` (byte-identical) | unchanged (no injection) | `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (byte-identical) |
| cpu-only | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |
| npu | generic: `torch.version.npu` (if provided), device count, device name | `try: import torch_npu` | `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` |
| other PrivateUse1 | generic collection | `try: import torch_<name>` | historical fallback |

Every in-tree backend (cuda/cpu/xpu/mps/mtia) lands on the verbatim fallback path — cpu-args and cuda-args repros are byte-identical before/after this patch (A/B diff verified on the validation boxes).

## Depends on

None. All APIs used (`torch._C._get_privateuse1_backend_name()`, `torch.cuda.device_count()`, `getattr(torch.version, <dt>)`) are already in trunk.

## Not changed

- `_cuda_system_info_comment` in `debug_utils.py` is untouched and remains the collector for cpu/cuda repros. When the debug_utils device-agnostic entry point lands, this module can switch to it with a one-line change (follow-up).
- `_dynamo/device_interface.py` and the inductor registration paths are untouched.
- The unused `_build_symbolic_wrapper` helper's `a.is_cuda` is left as-is (dead code, see the NOTE in source) — identified during review and moved out of scope for this PR.
- The mapping constant is a `TODO(#189137)` placeholder for `visible_devices_env()`.
- `torch_npu` requires no changes: the helpers only use standard `torch.npu.is_available/device_count/get_device_name`, and `_get_privateuse1_backend_name()` already covers PrivateUse1.

## Test plan

- NPU (Ascend 910B3 x8, torch 2.13.0a0+gitfad7424 + torch_npu 2.13.0): probe `generate_compiler_repro_string(gm, [npu_tensor])` on base -> no `import torch_npu`, header shows `no GPU info collected`; after patch -> injection present + `# npu device count: 8` + `# npu device 0: Ascend910B3`. Runner -> OK (13 tests). `test_debug_utils.py` regression -> 48 passed / 4 failed with the failure set byte-identical to the unpatched base (pre-existing, see Notes). cpu-args repro byte-identical before/after (A/B diff).
- CPU (venv_cpu, `cuda=False`): runner -> OK (13 tests); `test_debug_utils.py` regression -> 36 passed.
- CUDA (node-5-15, 4x A100-SXM4-80GB, CUDA 12.4): cuda-args repro byte-identical before/after the patch (`CUDA NO-OP VERIFIED`); runner -> OK (13 tests); `test_debug_utils.py` regression -> 67 passed.
- CI (lint / unittest / dynamo shards).

## Notes (pre-existing failures, not introduced by this PR)

1. `test/dynamo/test_debug_utils.py`: 4 cases fail identically on the unpatched runtime tree. Two root causes, both in the torch_npu patch layer: (a) `TestInductorConfigOverrideIntegrationCPU` x2 — one fails with `TypeError: patch_inductor_wrapper.<locals>.new_call() got an unexpected keyword argument 'config_patches'` (trunk's compiler wrapper now passes `config_patches=`; torch_npu's patched `new_call` is stale), the other hits an import-time `RuntimeError: 0 active drivers ([]). There should only be one.` from `torch_npu/_inductor/config.py` initializing the triton driver inside the patched cudagraph check; (b) `TestBackendOverrideIntegrationNPU` x2 — `KeyError: 'npu'` from `device_op_overrides_dict` (no OOT registration channel; upstream RFC #189137 proposes these registration interfaces). None are touched by this diff. Ownership: (a) torch_npu, (b) the #189137 RFC scope. Not fixing here to keep the diff scoped to `after_aot.py`.
2. Running a generated npu repro end-to-end (`get_args`) hits a SyntaxError: torch_npu's runtime patch of `InputWriter.tensor` emits kwargs containing slashes (`origin_format_/ND=True, ...`), which are not valid Python identifiers. Proven pre-existing by A/B: the unpatched base produces the same error at the same line, and the base-vs-patched generated scripts differ only in this PR's two header changes — the `reader.tensor(...)` line is byte-identical. Ownership: torch_npu (InputWriter patch layer). Not fixing here; a torch_npu-side fix would unlock full end-to-end npu repro validation (tracked with the torch_npu team).

title: [Dynamo] route PrivateUse1 autocast classes
body:
Dynamo recognizes the built-in autocast context managers, but an autocast
  subclass exposed by a registered PrivateUse1 device module can otherwise fall
  through to the user-defined class path. This prevents the context manager from
  being represented as an AutocastModeVariable during tracing.

  This change resolves `torch.<registered_backend>.amp.autocast` through the
  registered device module and routes the exact registered class through
  `TorchCtxManagerClassVariable`.

  The lookup first rejects ordinary functions and unrelated classes before
  accessing the registered device module. Class matching uses identity only;
  there is no source-file or qualified-name fallback.

  When reconstructing the context:

  - `device_type` is supplied from the registered backend only when the wrapper
    signature does not expose it.
  - An explicitly supplied `device_type` is preserved.
  - Missing `dtype`, `enabled`, and `cache_enabled` values use the base autocast
    defaults instead of raising an internal `KeyError`.

  The open registration tests exercise the actual `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`
  routing path. Reduced-signature behavior is covered by a temporary registered
  test class, leaving the existing open registration wrapper API unchanged.

  This does not add a `DeviceInterface` slot, backend-specific metadata, or a new
  trace rule.

title: Fix no-tensor-aliasing recompile reason for stale sources
body:

* __->__ #184793

NO_TENSOR_ALIASING guard failure reporting re-evaluates the tensor source
expressions recorded by the first compile. When a later invocation changes a
container that held tensors into a value such as None, sources like

reporting, while unavailable sources are included in a separate reason.
TypeError handling is limited to subscription/indexing failures so unrelated
evaluation bugs still propagate.

recompile reason actionable and preserves information about the stale guard
sources.

title: Make FX traceback preserve state thread-local
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #184917

FX traceback stored preservation flags and metadata in module globals. A
preserve_node_meta or sequence-number context in one thread therefore changed
what concurrent tracing work observed, leaking metadata across threads.

Move the state behind one Python thread-local object while preserving the
existing mutable current_meta interface and boolean behavior. Python TLS alone
is not captured by autograd's C++ ThreadLocalState, so publish the caller's
live state through ThreadLocalPythonObjects while a preservation context is
active. This lets a GraphTask snapshot see metadata updates made after context
entry.

A native snapshot initially shares its Python object with the caller. Lazily
copy and re-stash the state on the first mutable access whose GraphTask ID does
not match its marker. GraphTask.thread_locals_ retains the original seed, so
the engine reinstalls a mismatching seed for each NodeTask and each NodeTask
gets a private copy. Reentrant GraphTasks similarly fork from the active outer
state. ThreadLocalStateGuard restores the prior native object on success or
exception and keeps posthook metadata alive through InputBuffer.add. This also
isolates mutations from tensor or user prehooks that run before the AOT
traceback prehook.

Ordinary caller tracing skips native object-map probes when no GraphTask is
active, and TracerBase.create_node snapshots the combined state once to avoid
repeated TLS lookups on the FX hot path. The process-global callback_set
workaround is removed because native TLS restoration now owns cleanup and the
global set was itself racy.

Fixes #173816

title: [ROCm] Honor depthwise_kernel="native" where the native kernel applies
body:
torch.backends.cudnn.flags(depthwise_kernel=...) is only consulted inside use_cudnn_depthwise(), which returns false when cuDNN is absent. On ROCm _select_conv_backend then took the next branch and picked MiopenDepthwise for "auto", "cudnn" and "native" alike, so asking for the native depthwise kernel had no effect unless MIOpen was disabled altogether. That is also why test_Conv2d_depthwise_kernel_flag was skipped on ROCm: all three modes ran the same kernel, so the comparison was meaningless.

The MIOpen depthwise branch now goes through ConvParams::use_miopen_depthwise(), which skips MIOpen when the flag is NATIVE and the native kernel can actually serve the input. "auto" and "cudnn" keep MIOpen unchanged.

What the native kernel can serve is taken from that kernel rather than from cuDNN's predicate. It is 2-D only, so a 5-D depthwise convolution stays on MIOpen: conv_depthwise3d has never run for fp32, fp16 or bf16 on ROCm, carries tighter numel <= INT32_MAX limits, and stages its grad_weight block reduction in scalar_t after accumulating in accscalar_t. It also indexes with 32 bits, and the tensors it range-checks are the input and the output, not the weight, in all three directions: the forward checks input and output, grad_input checks grad_input and grad_output, and grad_weight checks input and grad_output. A channel multiplier makes the output k times the size of the input, so an input just under INT_MAX can produce an output over it; the guard therefore tests input, weight and output element counts, taking the output count from conv_output_size(). Element counts are sufficient here because the backend contiguous-ifies before the kernel runs. Finally, a channels-last input stays on MIOpen when MIOpen is the one asked to suggest NHWC.

The remaining conditions cuDNN applies are deliberately not mirrored. On CUDA the flag is consulted only inside kernel_cond, which additionally requires fp16, at least 32 channels, no dilation and a square or 1-D stride, because those are the shapes cuDNN has a depthwise kernel for. MIOpen serves every dtype use_miopen() accepts and the native kernel handles all of them correctly, so "native" is a wider switch on ROCm than on CUDA.

With the test comparing two different kernels, fp16 needs a wider tolerance on ROCm. For fp16 depthwise 3x3 MIOpen selects the Winograd solver ConvBinWinogradRxSf2x3, whose output against an exact fp64 reference is off by up to 4.1e-3 over 50 seeds (about two fp16 steps at these magnitudes), while the native kernel stays at 9.8e-4; that gap is the same on gfx950, gfx942 and gfx90a and is reported as ROCm/rocm-libraries#12334. Across 500 seeds the largest MIOpen-to-native difference was 5.9e-3, so the ROCm atol is 1e-2; CUDA keeps 1e-3.

The tolerance is not what makes the test meaningful. Comparing numerics alone cannot fail in the state the test exists to catch: when "native" is not honored, all three modes run the same deterministic MIOpen kernel and return bitwise identical tensors, which passes at any tolerance. The test now asserts the selected backend, and a second test covers the 2-D restriction.

Test Plan:

On gfx950 (MI355X, ROCm 10.0), 533 passed, 343 skipped, 24 xfailed:

```
python -m pytest test/nn/test_convolution.py -k "depthwise or Depthwise or conv_backend"
```

Backend selection on a 4-D contiguous input returns CudaDepthwise2d for "native" and MiopenDepthwise for "auto" and "cudnn". A 5-D input stays on MiopenDepthwise under "native". A channel multiplier whose output exceeds INT_MAX while its input does not stays on MiopenDepthwise and runs, where routing it to the native kernel instead fails that kernel's own canUse32BitIndexMath(input) && canUse32BitIndexMath(output) check. torch.compile(dynamic=True) with the flag set matches eager across several batch sizes.

The tolerance measurements above were repeated on gfx942 and gfx90a, where MIOpen picked the same Winograd solver with the same 4.12e-3 error, so the fp16 gap is a property of the solver rather than of one architecture. The backend-selection changes have been exercised on gfx950 only.

This PR was authored with the assistance of an AI agent (Claude). The analysis and test results were verified by hand.

title: [dynamo] Lower the backward eagerly under the multi-graph capture config
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #198217
* #198227
* #198138
* #198216
* #198137
* __->__ #198215
* #198136
* #198214
* #198243
* #198135
* #198213
* #197993
* #198284
* #198283
* #198223
* #198211

**Problem.** `_capture_config` only forced the backward to lower eagerly for `training=True`, but AOTAutograd does not save a grad-enabled graph to the bundled cache until its backward has been lowered, so an ordinary inference capture made outside `torch.no_grad()` compiled fine and then had nothing to put in the artifact.

**Fix.** Set `force_non_lazy_backward_lowering` unconditionally in the capture config and drop the `training` parameter it used to gate on.

**Summary.** `_capture_config(training)` added `force_non_lazy_backward_lowering` to its functorch patch only when `training=True`, leaving inference captures with AOTAutograd's default of lowering a graph's backward lazily on the first `.backward()`. The cache entry the bundled artifact is built from is saved only once the backward has been lowered, so a graph compiled with grad enabled whose backward was never lowered records no backend at all -- and that is the ordinary inference case, a capture made outside `torch.no_grad()` on a model whose parameters require grad. The flag is now set unconditionally, so a graph compiled with grad enabled carries its backward into the artifact, and a call served under that grad mode returns outputs with a `grad_fn` as eager does. A call made under `torch.no_grad()` still compiles an inference graph, because the flag only changes when a backward that AOTAutograd would build anyway gets lowered, not whether one exists. With nothing left for it to select, the `training` parameter goes, and the two `_capture_config` tests pin the unconditional flag and its scoping.

## Where this fits

The stack replaces the callable `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` (trace once on inputs passed up front, pair returned in memory) with a caller-driven context manager: `capture(fn, artifact_path=, cache_path=)` is entered with a `with` block, the caller calls it on as many example inputs as they like (each graph break and recompiled variant is folded in), the `(python_code, cache)` pair is written to the two files on exit, and `load(artifact_path, cache_path)` serves it in a fresh process. The end-to-end example and the PR-by-PR map live in #197993's "The new API, end to end" section. This PR is plumbing for the multi-call `DynamoTracer` capture (#198138): the capture config always lowers the backward eagerly, so a grad-enabled call records its artifact.

## The patch dict, before and after

The parent built the functorch patch and then appended the eager-lowering flag under a condition:

```python
# parent: torch/_dynamo/precompile_package.py
@contextlib.contextmanager
def _capture_config(training: bool) -> Iterator[None]:
    functorch_patch = {
        "bundled_autograd_cache": True,
        "bypass_autograd_cache_key": True,
    }
    if training:
        functorch_patch["force_non_lazy_backward_lowering"] = True
    ...
```

Now the flag is part of the dict itself and the parameter is gone:

```python
# now
@contextlib.contextmanager
def _capture_config() -> Iterator[None]:
    functorch_patch = {
        "bundled_autograd_cache": True,
        "force_non_lazy_backward_lowering": True,
        "bypass_autograd_cache_key": True,
    }
    ...
```

The rest of the scope is unchanged: `strict_autograd_cache` still follows `torch._dynamo.config.strict_precompile`, `allow_empty_graphs` is still patched on, and `force_disable_caches` still raises `PackageError` up front. The docstring now says why the backward lowers eagerly for every capture: a graph compiled with grad enabled whose backward was never lowered is never saved, so a capture that never makes one -- a training step, or an inference call made outside `torch.no_grad()` -- would record no backend at all.

## Why an inference capture was affected

AOTAutograd lowers a graph's backward lazily, on the first `.backward()`, and the bundled cache entry is saved only once that has happened. A capture that only runs forwards never triggers the lowering:

```python
model = torch.nn.Linear(4, 4)          # parameters require grad
with _capture_config(training=False):  # parent: no eager lowering
    compiled(model, x)                 # grad enabled -> joint graph, backward deferred
# parent: no .backward() ever ran, so the entry was never saved -> no backend in the artifact
# now:    the backward is lowered at compile time, the entry is saved, the artifact has a backend
```

Under `torch.no_grad()` there is no backward to lower, so that path compiles an inference graph exactly as before.

## Tests

Both `_capture_config` tests move to the parameterless call and pin the flag as unconditional. `test_capture_config_is_scoped_per_entry_and_per_thread` reads the four patched flags in order (`bundled_autograd_cache`, `bypass_autograd_cache_key`, `force_non_lazy_backward_lowering`, `allow_empty_graphs`) from an all-`False` ambient:

```python
# parent
with _capture_config(training=False):
    self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, False, True))
    with _capture_config(training=True):
        self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, True, True))
    self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, False, True))

# now
with _capture_config():
    self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, True, True))
    with _capture_config():
        self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, True, True))
    self.assertEqual(flags(), (True, True, True, True))
self.assertEqual(flags(), ambient)
```

The same test still checks that an exception inside the scope restores the ambient flags, and that a worker thread holding its own `_capture_config()` scope sees `(True, True, True, True)` while the main thread's flags are untouched. `test_capture_config_refuses_disabled_caches_and_honours_strict` keeps its `force_disable_caches` refusal and its `strict_precompile` -> `strict_autograd_cache` checks, now written as `with _capture_config():`.

Test Plan:

```

lintrunner -a torch/_dynamo/precompile_package.py test/dynamo/test_precompile_package.py
```

title: [dynamo] Render a PrecompileSession as an artifact behind the coverage and guard gates
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #198217
* #198227
* #198138
* __->__ #198216
* #198137
* #198215
* #198136
* #198214
* #198243
* #198135
* #198213
* #197993
* #198284
* #198283
* #198223
* #198211

**Problem.** A `PrecompileSession` can capture calls and report on them through `summary()`, but nothing turns what it captured into the `(python_code, cache)` artifact, so a caller-driven capture still cannot produce anything to save or load.

**Fix.** Add `PrecompileSession.snapshot_artifact()`, which runs the coverage and guard gates, gathers the compiled subgraphs by backend id, and hands them to `_build_multigraph_artifact`, while leaving the session open so a caller can checkpoint mid-block.

**Summary.** The parent commit's `PrecompileSession` runs the caller's calls under `_capture_config` and the wrapped guard filter and exposes `summary()`, but its docstring still says "Rendering the artifact is the next commit's", so a capture had no way to become an artifact. This commit adds `snapshot_artifact()`, which renders everything captured SO FAR as the `(python_code, cache)` pair and leaves the session able to capture more, which is what lets a caller checkpoint mid-block. It runs the gates first, through `_gated_summary`, so a refusal renders nothing: `require_no_dropped_guards` refuses any dropped guard, `require_no_risky_drops` the risky subset the summary reports, and `require_complete` a capture whose call raised, that compiled no code or no graph, or that left a frame uncovered or bypassed, and it refuses any other incomplete summary as a backstop; each refusal names the remedy and the flag that accepts the gap. `_collect_backends` then gathers the compiled subgraphs by backend id -- the bundled AOTAutograd entries taken from `PrecompileContext` for inductor, the captured fx graphs and `noop_graph_call` wrapped as `EagerCacheArtifact`s for eager -- and names any id without a serializable artifact rather than writing an artifact that would fail at load. The defaults are `require_complete=True`, `require_no_risky_drops=True`, `require_no_dropped_guards=False`, so a capture with only harmless dropped guards renders, and `test_precompile_session_renders_behind_the_gates`, parametrized over the eager and inductor backends, pins the mid-block render, the after-exit render, and each refusal.

## Where this fits

The stack replaces the callable `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` (trace once on inputs passed up front, pair returned in memory) with a caller-driven context manager: `capture(fn, artifact_path=, cache_path=)` is entered with a `with` block, the caller calls it on as many example inputs as they like (each graph break and recompiled variant is folded in), the `(python_code, cache)` pair is written to the two files on exit, and `load(artifact_path, cache_path)` serves it in a fresh process. The end-to-end example and the PR-by-PR map live in #197993's "The new API, end to end" section. This PR renders a `PrecompileSession` as an artifact behind the coverage and guard gates; `capture(..., tracer=DynamoTracer())` (#198138) writes through it.

## Rendering mid-block and after exit

`snapshot_artifact()` does not finish the session. The test runs under `@parametrize("backend", ["eager", "inductor"])`; its fixture graph-breaks once, so each call produces two frames, and the mid-block render already shows both:

```python
def step(model, x):
    y = model(x)
    torch._dynamo.graph_break()
    return y.sum(dim=0) + y.shape[0]

model = torch.nn.Linear(4, 4)
session = precompile_package.precompile_capture(step, backend=backend)   # "eager" or "inductor"
with session as call:
    call(model, torch.ones(2, 4))
    python_code, cache = session.snapshot_artifact()   # mid-block checkpoint
    len(_parse_artifact_metadata(python_code)["FRAMES"])  # 2; the session stays open
    call(model, torch.ones(3, 4))                        # a second variant still captures
summary = session.summary()
python_code, cache = session.snapshot_artifact()         # after exit, renders both variants
```

The rendered metadata agrees with the summary: `meta["TRACER"] == "dynamo"`, `meta["FN_NAME"] == step.__qualname__`, `sum(n for _, n in meta["FRAMES"]) == summary.guarded_codes`, `meta["DROPPED_GUARDS"] == [list(s) for s in summary.dropped_guards]`, and `torch.load(io.BytesIO(cache), weights_only=True)` carries `(backend, "dynamo")` as its `backend` and `tracer` tag. Under inductor every backend graph is a bundled entry the session takes out of `PrecompileContext`, so the after-exit render only passes if the second render still finds the artifacts of the variants the first render already collected; under eager the fx graphs themselves are the artifacts. The `snapshot_artifact` docstring also records a precondition: under inductor the cache half bundles whatever `CacheArtifactManager` recorded, so the session should run under `with_fresh_cache()` (as `capture()` does) to keep the bundle to this session's compiles. The rendering itself is unchanged code, `_build_multigraph_artifact(self._package.cache_entry(), backends, summary, self._backend, self._fn)`.

## The gates run first, so a refusal renders nothing

`_gated_summary` takes the three keyword flags and checks them against `summary()` in order, raising `PackageError` with the remedy and the flag that accepts the gap:

```python
summary = self.summary()
if require_no_dropped_guards and summary.dropped_guards:
    raise PackageError(...)   # any dropped guard; "pass require_no_dropped_guards=False to accept the default policy"
if require_no_risky_drops and summary.risky_dropped_guards:
    raise PackageError(...)   # the risky subset: a slot whose value differed between variants,
                              # a configuration-dependent identity slot, or a custom-filter drop
if require_complete:
    if summary.capture_errors: ...       # a captured call raised
    if summary.guarded_codes == 0: ...   # nothing was run inside the block
    if summary.backend_graphs == 0: ...  # every captured frame was empty
    if summary.uncovered_frames: ...     # a frame produced no guarded code (dispatch-only, or a graph break)
    if summary.bypassed: ...             # a frame whose guards could not be serialized
    # Backstop: the branches above only add detail, and any reason they
    # do not name (a truncated frame) still refuses.
    if not summary.complete:
        raise PackageError(
            f"Precompilation is incomplete: {summary}. Pass "
            "require_complete=False to save the partial artifact."
        )
return summary
```

The per-reason branches only make the message specific; the final `summary.complete` check is what guarantees that no incomplete summary slips through, including a reason none of them names. Truncation is the example: `PrecompileSummary` carries a `truncated` field, but sessions never report truncation yet (`summary()` passes `truncated=frozenset()`), so today the backstop only guards against a future reason. Only after the summary passes does `snapshot_artifact` collect backends and render, so a refused capture never writes a partial `python_code`. The same session from above exercises the strict-drop gate and the completeness gate, and a separate eager session exercises the risky-drop gate:

```python
# The default policy renders: the eager capture dropped only harmless guards.
python_code, cache = session.snapshot_artifact()
# The strict gate refuses those same drops.
with self.assertRaisesRegex(PackageError, "dropped .* guard"):
    session.snapshot_artifact(require_no_dropped_guards=True)

# A session that never ran its callable has nothing to render.
empty = precompile_package.precompile_capture(step, backend="eager")
with empty:
    pass
with self.assertRaisesRegex(PackageError, "no compiled code"):
    empty.snapshot_artifact()

# A session whose call raised is incomplete unless the caller accepts it.
failed = precompile_package.precompile_capture(step, backend="eager")
with failed as call:
    call(model, torch.ones(2, 4))
    with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
        call(model, torch.ones(2, 5))   # Linear(4, 4) rejects a width-5 input
with self.assertRaisesRegex(PackageError, "captured call raised"):
    failed.snapshot_artifact()
python_code, _ = failed.snapshot_artifact(require_complete=False)   # the partial artifact

# The risky-drop gate is on by default; a custom filter's drop is risky.
default = precompile_package.default_guard_filter_fn
custom = precompile_package.precompile_capture(
    step,
    backend="eager",
    guard_filter_fn=lambda es: [keep and e.name != "x" for keep, e in zip(default(es), es)],
)
with custom as call:
    call(model, torch.ones(2, 4))
with self.assertRaisesRegex(PackageError, "can affect dispatch"):
    custom.snapshot_artifact()                        # the dropped tensor guard on `x` is risky
custom.snapshot_artifact(require_no_risky_drops=False)   # accepted explicitly, renders
```

The custom filter keeps everything `default_guard_filter_fn` keeps except the tensor guard on `x`, so the only difference from the default-policy session is one drop that came from a custom filter, and that alone is enough for the default-on risky-drop gate to refuse.

## Collecting the backends by id

`_collect_backends` first calls `_take_backend_artifacts()` to move this capture's bundled AOTAutograd entries out of `PrecompileContext`, then walks `entry.backend_ids` in sorted order:

```python
for backend_id in sorted(entry.backend_ids):
    artifact = self._backend_artifacts.get(backend_id)      # inductor: the bundled AOTAutograd entry
    backend = self._package.cached_backends.get(backend_id)
    if artifact is None and backend is not None:
        if self._backend == "eager" or backend is noop_graph_call:
            artifact = EagerCacheArtifact(key=backend_id, content=backend)  # eager: the fx graph itself
    if artifact is None:
        missing.append(backend_id)
    else:
        collected[str(backend_id)] = artifact
```

An eager "backend" is an fx graph with no compiled artifact of its own, and `output_graph` short-circuits an empty graph to `noop_graph_call` without filing anything under its id even though the bytecode still names it; both are carried as-is. Any id left without an artifact is named rather than written, because an artifact missing a subgraph would fail at load instead of here:

```python
if missing:
    raise PackageError(
        f"precompile captured {len(entry.backend_ids)} backend graph(s) but "
        f"{len(missing)} of them recorded no serializable artifact: {missing}. "
        f"The {self._backend!r} backend reaches the artifact through the AOTAutograd "
        f"cache (bundled_autograd_cache); a graph that cache bypassed cannot be served. "
        f"Check TORCH_LOGS=+aot for the bypass reason."
    )
```

## Tests

`test_precompile_session_renders_behind_the_gates`, under both the eager and inductor backends, renders mid-block and after exit, checks the parsed metadata and the cache tag against the summary, and exercises the strict-drop gate, the risky-drop gate with a filter that drops a tensor guard, an empty session, and a session whose call raised with and without `require_complete`. The `PrecompileSession` docstring now points at `snapshot_artifact` instead of deferring rendering to the next commit.

Test Plan:

`test_precompile_session_renders_behind_the_gates`, under both the eager and inductor backends, renders mid-block and after exit, checks the parsed metadata and the cache tag against the summary, and exercises the strict-drop gate, the risky-drop gate with a filter that drops a tensor guard, an empty session, and a session whose call raised with and without `require_complete`.

lintrunner -a torch/_dynamo/precompile_package.py test/dynamo/test_precompile_package.py
```

title: [inductor] Fold small-row expanded bmm to mm in post-grad
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #185404

A dynamic linear on batch-first transposed activations can reach post-grad as
an expanded batched matmul:

    [T, B, K] @ expand([K, N], [T, K, N])

For small B this produces many small-row GEMMs. On CUDA fp16 this path can be
much slower than flattening the transposed activation to [T * B, K] and using
one mm. The issue shows up in AOTInductor autocast because the fp16 cast drops
requires_grad, so the existing matmul folding heuristic no longer takes the
requires_grad escape hatch that the fp32 graph happened to use.

Add a post-grad Inductor pattern for the specific expanded-bmm shape generated
by transposed linear. This keeps eager and general decomposition stride behavior
unchanged, addressing the concern from the abandoned decomposition-only PR. The
pattern is deliberately narrow: GPU fp16/bf16/fp32, batch-first transpose
layout, large T/K/N, and B <= 64. Dynamic dimensions are checked with guards so
cache reuse is stable: large batches keep the original bmm path, while small
batches compile to the mm path.

I considered a runtime torch.cond between bmm and mm, but tracing cond inside
this post-grad replacement currently nests torch.compile and trips Inductor's
compile event stack. Guarded specialization is the simpler established path and
keeps large-batch behavior on the original implementation.

Benchmark Results:
On NVIDIA B200, fp16, T=1000, K=2048, N=6144, max_autotune_gemm_backends=ATEN,
5 warmup iterations and 20 timed CUDA-event iterations:

Before:
- B=1: current bmm 0.0721 ms, manual folded mm 0.0724 ms
- B=2: current bmm 1.3912 ms, manual folded mm 0.0841 ms
- B=4: current bmm 1.4169 ms, manual folded mm 0.1524 ms

After:
- generated code uses mm for the small-batch guarded graph
- B=1: 0.0772 ms
- B=2: 0.0903 ms
- B=4: 0.1531 ms

Test Plan:
- python test/inductor/test_pattern_matcher.py -k test_transposed_linear_dynamic_batch_uses_guarded_mm

title: [Test] Add has_sufficient_memory() hook to DeviceTypeTestBase
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a `has_sufficient_memory()` hook to `DeviceTypeTestBase` and updates `largeTensorTest()` to use it when available.

It also introduces `test_size_overrides` to allow device-specific test bases to override declared test sizes.

## Motivation

`largeTensorTest()` currently relies on `_has_sufficient_memory()` to determine whether a device has enough available memory for a requested allocation size. `_has_sufficient_memory()` currently contains hardcoded backend-specific memory queries for built-in device types such as CUDA/XPU/MPS/CPU.

Available memory querying is fundamentally a device-level capability and is useful for device-generic testing infrastructure.

Additionally, out-of-tree backends may need to override the memory requirements declared by `largeTensorTest()` to accommodate backend-specific memory constraints.

This PR introduces a reusable `has_sufficient_memory()` hook on `DeviceTypeTestBase` so device-specific test bases can customize memory reporting behavior.

## Changes

- Add `has_sufficient_memory()` hook to `DeviceTypeTestBase`
- Implement the hook for CPU/CUDA/MPS/XPU test bases.
- Update `largeTensorTest()` to use the hook when available while preserving the existing fallback logic for compatibility.
-  Add `test_size_overrides` to allow device-specific test bases to override memory requirements declared by `largeTensorTest()`. 
- Add OpenReg test cases to verify the memory hook and test size overrides.



## Test Plan

title: Fix reinplace alias checks for index_put
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #185450

Inductor's reinplace pass can rewrite functional index_put into its in-place variant when the destination has no later observable uses. That check was only reasoning about later uses of the destination tensor. It did not account for operands that index_put reads during the operation.

When self aliases either the values tensor or a tensor entry in the indices list, rewriting aten.index_put.default to aten.index_put_.default changes a functional update into an in-place read/write overlap. That is unsafe: eager either needs functional clone semantics or raises the usual overlap error for the in-place form. The same hazard applies to the _unsafe_index_put mapping, and the extra_check hook also has to handle with_effects nodes where inner op arguments are shifted by the token and op operands.

This adds an index_put-specific reinplace eligibility check that rejects overlap between self and all read tensor operands: values plus every tensor nested in indices. The check is shared by aten.index_put.default and aten._unsafe_index_put.default, and it accounts for with_effects positional argument offsets.

An older abandoned draft PR for #156786 only checked the last positional argument, which misses schemas with an accumulate argument and does not cover indices. This version keys off the operator schema positions instead.

Fixes #156786

title: Functionalize mutations in deferred local_map
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.16.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #185043

Deferred local_map builds its joint forward/backward graph from an already captured local body while functionalization is suspended. Mutation nodes can therefore survive into partitioning, and side-effect-only Triton mutation HOPs can be dropped entirely under FakeTensor execution. A raw joint trace can also fail when an in-place update changes a tensor that an earlier operator saved for backward.

Materialize a forward-only graph first so call_method, mutable ATen, out=, Python wrapper, and mutation-HOP forms are visible. For supported non-invoke bodies, functionalize that forward before AD tracing, using an explicit empty make_fx decomposition table so detach boundaries survive into the later backward. Bodies containing opaque Python callables stay on the AD-aware path so a hidden custom autograd function keeps its backward semantics. Only the exact torch package namespace is treated as internal, so third-party packages such as torchao do not accidentally take the pre-AD path.

invoke_subgraph needs Python-mode functionalization but saves operands for lazy backward construction. Give inspection and joint traces fresh cache identifiers, and use stride-preserving operand clones only while building its mutation-bearing joint. After custom autograd and nested HOP backward logic has expanded, functionalize the canonical joint before partitioning. Effectful or still-unsupported HOP combinations fail explicitly instead of silently miscompiling.

Pre-functionalizing every body was rejected because it can erase custom autograd boundaries, while post-joint-only functionalization can hit saved-tensor version checks before it gets a graph. The split path preserves AD semantics while normalizing mutations early whenever that is safe.

Fixes #167568
